structure.overview: Ms. XXXX, a Somali citizen, appealed the Refugee Protection Division's (RPD) denial of refugee protection. The Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) reviewed new evidence regarding her identity and the risk she faces as a single woman in Somalia. The RAD allowed the appeal, finding Ms. XXXX to be a Convention refugee due to a serious possibility of persecution upon return to Somalia.

party_points.text: RPD erred in finding Ms. XXXX did not establish her personal identity
Submitted new evidence including Somali birth certificate, Ethiopian school record, and affidavits
Made reasonable efforts to connect with family and community; school record credible despite minor errors
Ms. XXXX is a Convention refugee as a single woman facing persecution without family support
Ms. XXXX lacks clan and male support and likely will not be protected by clan if returned
Single women in Somalia face discrimination and widespread gender-based violence without protection

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The appeal by Ms. XXXX, a Somali citizen, against the RPD's denial of refugee protection is allowed and she is found to be a Convention refugee.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Ms. XXXX fled Somalia to Ethiopia in 2006 after her father's death, then left Ethiopia in 2018 due to conflict, arriving alone in Canada and losing contact with family.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The main issue is whether the RPD erred in finding Ms. XXXX did not establish her personal identity; the court finds the RPD erred and accepts new evidence establishing identity.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court independently reviewed all evidence and applied Chairperson Guidelines on women fearing gender-related persecution in making its decision.
idea_list: court's independent review and guideline application

citations.cite: Chairperson Guidelines 4: Women Refugee Claimants Fearing Gender-Related Persecution

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The RAD may accept new evidence only if it meets section 110(4) IRPA criteria and is credible, relevant, and arose after the RPD decision or was unavailable before.
idea_list: criteria for accepting new evidence at RAD

citations.why: sets criteria for new evidence acceptance

citations.cite: section 110(4) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act

citations.why: evidence must be credible and trustworthy

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Ms. XXXX submitted new evidence including a Somali birth certificate, Ethiopian school record, and three affidavits from relatives and friends living in Edmonton.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court accepts the Ethiopian school record and the affidavit from Ms. XXXX's distant relative as new evidence at the RAD.
idea_list: acceptance of two new evidence items

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Somali birth certificate is found untrustworthy due to lack of verification, common document fraud, and no national birth registration system, so it is rejected.

citations.why: explains birth certificate issuance issues in Somalia

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Ethiopian school record is accepted as new evidence because it was not reasonably available before the RPD decision and corroborates Ms. XXXX's testimony.
idea_list: school record not available before RPD
disagrees with RPD on efforts to establish identity

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Ms. XXXX made reasonable efforts to connect with family and community, and the school record is credible despite minor errors and relevant to her identity.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The affidavit from Ms. XXXX's distant relative is accepted as new evidence because it was not reasonably available and is credible and relevant.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Two affidavits from friends known to Ms. XXXX before the RPD decision are rejected as new evidence because she did not make reasonable efforts to locate them.
idea_list: rejection of two affidavits due to availability and lack of effort

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: No oral hearing is held as the accepted new evidence is credible, uncontradicted, and does not raise serious credibility issues.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Ms. XXXX has established her national and personal identity on a balance of probabilities based on accepted evidence and credible testimony.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Ms. XXXX is a Convention refugee as a single woman returning to Somalia without family support, facing a serious possibility of persecution.
idea_list: finding of refugee status based on social group

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Ms. XXXX is credible, has not been to Somalia since childhood, has no family network there, and has a grade XXXX education level.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Somali culture and religion oppose women living alone; single women without male support face denial of justice and must rely on male and clan protection.
idea_list: cultural context of women's vulnerability in Somalia

citations.why: explains cultural and religious norms affecting women

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Ms. XXXX lacks clan and male support and may be seen as having broken social norms, so she likely will not be protected by her clan if returned to Somalia.
idea_list: lack of protection due to clan and social norms

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Single women in Somalia face discrimination in housing, employment, loans, and widespread gender-based violence without protection.
idea_list: discrimination and violence against single women

citations.why: details discrimination and violence against women in Somalia

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Considering country conditions and Ms. XXXX's circumstances, the court finds she faces persecution and lacks an internal flight alternative in Somalia.
idea_list: persecution risk and no internal flight alternative

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The appeal is allowed and the court substitutes its decision that Ms. XXXX is a Convention refugee.

citations.cite: 1951 Convention Relating to the Status of Refugees
Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada, Guidelines Issued by the Chairperson
Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA), S.C. 2001, c. 27
Canada (Citizenship and Immigration) v. Singh, 2016 FCA 96
